To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

it is technically feasible to use multiplanar and three-dimensional (3D)-reconstructed images from computed tomographic ( CT ) data obtained for maternal indications to visualize fetal anatomy and estimate gestational age at fetal doses much lower than those that would cause harm.

it is technically feasible to create clinically useful fetal images using multiplanar reconstruc-tions and three-dimensional (3D)-reconstructed data obtained during CT scanning of the pregnant abdomen.

it is technically feasible to use multiplanar and three-dimensional reconstructions of CT data from scans performed to evaluate maternal indications for visualizating fetal anatomy and estimating fetal age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of the parameters of the process of formation of a new generation of the population of the region on the structure of the population of a given age.
the use of CT for fetal imaging and the radiation doses associated with these examinations.
the study of the influence of the initial conditions on the behavior of the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CT is not indicated for fetal evaluation.

the use of multiplanar reconstruc- tions of CT data sets from pregnant patients for fetal imaging is technically feasible and may provide useful clinical information at fetal radiation doses much below the level that would be considered clinically actionable.
the use of CT for fetal imaging is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of multiplanar reconstruction (MPR) and 3-dimensional reconstruction (3DR) images from CT scans of pregnant patients performed for nonfetal reasons can be useful for fetal biometry and gross anatomic visualization.
CT is not a good modality for fetal imaging, but that it can provide useful information about the fetal anatomy and gestations age when used in the emergency department setting.
CT scanning of the abdomen for nonfetal indications can be used for fetal anatomic survey, and the estimated fetal radiation dose is low.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CT scan is a potential source of useful information about the fetal patient. © RSNA, 2016 Online supplemental material is available for this article.

the CT scan of a pregnant patient can provide useful information regarding the fetus, and that this can be obtained at fetal doses much lower than those that would be considered clinically significant.
